title: NEB Class 12 English — Grammar — 2021
origin: curated NEB-pattern set for class-12 English grammar

questions.question: Rewrite using the connector in brackets without changing the meaning: (a) He is rich. He is not happy. (although) (b) You must work hard. You will fail. (unless)
questions.solution:
(a) Concession with 'although' — the unexpected result goes in the main clause: Although he is rich, he is not happy. (Equivalently: He is not happy although he is rich.)
(b) 'Unless' means 'if … not', replacing the negative condition: You will fail unless you work hard. (The original 'must work hard' condition becomes the unless-clause; the consequence stays.)

questions.question: Put the verbs in the correct tense: (a) By this time tomorrow, I ___ (finish) my exams. (b) She ___ (work) here since 2015.
questions.solution:
(a) An action completed before a future point needs the future perfect: 'By this time tomorrow, I will have finished my exams.'
(b) An action starting in the past and continuing now needs the present perfect continuous: 'She has been working here since 2015.' ('Since' + starting point; 'for' would mark a duration.)

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence: (a) Its a beautiful day, isn't it. (b) It's a beautiful day, isn't it?
questions.solution: (b) is correct. 'It's' = 'it is' (the apostrophe marks the missing letter), while 'its' without an apostrophe is the possessive ('its colour'). The tag question 'isn't it?' needs its own comma and question mark.
